subject: Hosted API: monthly volume + peak burst confirmation
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Hosted API: monthly volume + peak burst confirmation

Hi Elena / Luke —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we align on the pricing inputs before I put a formal proposal together:

Summary of what I captured on the call:
- Primary use: in-product assistant for purchase & support flows (synchronous chat + short generation).
- Typical prompt size: 300-700 tokens per request (includes system + user + expected response).
- Expected active users: 18k monthly; not all concurrent but driving requests across business hours.

What I need to confirm (these are the inputs that materially affect hosted pricing):
1) Expected monthly tokens (total): you mentioned a ~200–300M token/month range — can you confirm a single number or a tighter range?
2) Peak TPS (requests/sec) and burst tolerance: you described spikes during promotions — what is the observed peak TPS and how long do bursts last?
3) Target unit economics: do you have a target $/1M tokens that makes this P&L work (or a monthly hosting budget range)?
4) Retention/latency SLOs: any hard latency targets for the assistant beyond typical sub-500ms token latency?

Next steps I propose:
- If you can send the CSV sample of a week of request timestamps (or the aggregated hourly rates), I’ll run a throughput simulation against our hosted pools.
- I’ll loop in pricing (Marissa) and infra (Karthik) to propose a couple of options: hosted pay-as-you-go vs. committed slab with burst capacity.

Attachments: feel free to attach the traffic sample — I included an SOW stub for reference but this is just a placeholder until we lock numbers.

If you can reply with the three bullets above (confirmed month tokens, peak TPS, budget band) I’ll aim to send a draft pricing memo within 48 hours.

Thanks —

Connor —

Great summary, thanks. Quick answers below and I attached the CSV you requested (hourly counts for last 7 days).

1) Monthly tokens: our finance model is currently forecasting 260,000,000 tokens/month as the midpoint for Q1. That includes a 10% growth buffer.
2) Peak TPS / bursts: normal steady-state TPS is ~18 TPS. Peak observed during product announcements was ~310 TPS sustained for ~6 minutes. We also see smaller spikes of 80–120 TPS for ~20–40s.
3) Budget: procurement asked us to target ~ $2,000–$3,500 per month for hosting initially — but engineering flagged that unit cost will determine feasibility. If you can show $/1M tokens and delta for committed slabs it will help.
4) Latency SLOs: soft target is 250–400ms p50 token latency; p95 ideally < 900ms.

Notes: the token estimate assumes average response lengths we discussed (~400 tokens). If our usage pattern forces larger responses we may need to revise.

Attaching: rapidfox_traffic_sample_nov.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API: monthly volume + peak burst confirmation — pricing ask

Connor —

Thanks for the clear inputs. Based on 260M tokens/mo and the burst profile, here are two realistic options to present. Numbers below are illustrative but use our recent unit economics and typical slab discounts.

Option A — Pay-as-you-go (no commit):
- Base unit: $45 per 1M tokens (hosted, on-demand)
- Estimated monthly: ~ $11,700 (260 * $45)
- Burst handling: autoscaling with transient capacity; small per-burst surcharge for provisioning (we can bake into usage).
- Pros: no commitment, fastest to start.
- Cons: significantly above RapidFox target band.

Option B — Committed slab (12-month, monthly billing)
- Slab: commit to 200M tokens/month baseline + 100M committed as flexible burst pool (effective coverage 300M with burst credits).
- Pricing: baseline at $28 per 1M tokens for the committed portion; additional committed-burst credits at $20 per 1M within agreed limits.
- Effective blended unit: ~ $25–$27 per 1M tokens depending on month-to-month usage mix.
- Estimated monthly: ~ $6,500–$7,000 (effective blended).
- Additional: short high-intensity bursts (<=10 minutes) covered by burst credits; longer sustained scaling will incur overage rates.

Recommendations / notes:
- To hit their $2k–$3.5k target we would need a much lower unit (<=$13/1M) or a marketing pilot subsidy — not sustainable at scale. Recommend we present Option B as the commercial starting point, and offer a 3-month pilot credit to de-risk; e.g., 50% off first month or $5k in platform credits.
- For the 310 TPS 6-minute spike, our infra team says burst credits + transient autoscale is the lowest friction approach. Karthik, if you think we should propose a dedicated short-burst reserve, advise on cost delta.

Next steps:
1) Connor: propose Option B in a 1-page commercial and include a pilot credit alternative.
2) Karthik: confirm infra feasibility and any implementation notes we should share with RapidFox (networking/KMS, ramp steps).
3) Procurement: if they push $/1M target, we'll evaluate a time-limited promotional piece.

I’ll draft a short commercial term sheet after Karthik confirms burst support.

—Marissa Cole
